clue.text: Little Nell's patronymic streamer

definitions.meaning: Little Nell, heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop
something that streams, i.e. a river; this one flows through the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A query about the family name of a Dickens heroine, oddly tacked onto a ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streamer' looks like a ribbon or pennant, but here it is a thing that streams: a river, the Trent of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell's surname in the novel is Trent, and the Trent is a major English river, a flowing watercourse.

clue.text: Knobbly underground girl

parts.note: the Tube is the everyday name for the London Underground railway

explanation.surface: A lumpy girl who lives below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective this word is a botanical variant of 'tuberous', meaning bearing tubers, lumpy; it is also the name of a scented flower, which the surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something covered in swellings or tubers, so lumpy and bumpy in outline.

clue.text: Modified real one is com" memorated at Charing Cross

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Some altered genuine figure honoured by a London monument.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward I put up crosses where the funeral procession of his queen rested; the one at Charing Cross, in central London, gave the place its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen consort of Edward I is remembered by the Victorian replica cross outside Charing Cross railway station.

clue.text: Barker from Yorkshire

definitions.meaning: a barker is a dog, especially a mongrel cur
a native of Yorkshire, the large county in northern England, is called by this nickname

explanation.surface: A loud-mouthed dog, or perhaps a market tout, hailing from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' suggests a fairground tout calling customers in; it is a dog. Yorkshire is a big county in the north of England whose people carry this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mongrel dog and, informally, a Yorkshireman.

clue.text: Taking no notice of gin blended twice with alternative ingredient

indicators.note: drinks blended together are mixed, so these letters are mixed into a new order
twice asks for the word gin to be used two times over in the mix

parts.note: or is the little word that introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone shrugging off a cocktail of gin, gin and another ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles GIN to give GINGIN; add OR and 'blended' rearranges all eight letters. 'Ingredient' just carries the cocktail picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention at all.

clue.text: Those proverbially infernal paving materials

parts.note: the proverb says the road to hell is paved with well-meant plans that were never carried out

explanation.definitionFit: The saying holds that hell's road is laid with kindly aims that come to nothing.

clue.text: They are not even chances for the better

definitions.meaning: numbers that are not even are uneven ones such as 1, 3 and 5
a better is one who bets, and the bookmaker quotes him the likelihood of a win as a price

explanation.surface: Uneven prospects that things might improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'improvement', but it is one who bets, and the bookmaker's prices are his chances.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneven numbers carry this name, and so do betting prices that express likelihood.

clue.text: Serial I edited as a Middle East citizen

indicators.note: a text that is edited gets reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A television serial cut about by an editor, featuring someone from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges only SERIAL; the I is kept at the end as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of the Jewish state on the eastern Mediterranean is a Middle Eastern citizen.

clue.text: Frivolous in a vertiginous way

definitions.meaning: frivolous means flighty or scatterbrained
vertiginous describes the dizzy, spinning feeling of vertigo

explanation.surface: Someone light-headed both in temperament and in balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both flighty and dizzy, as when the head swims from height.

clue.text: Enchanting tuition?

parts.note: enchanting is read as casting spells, so the tuition is a class in casting them, while the real class teaches how words are written

explanation.definitionFit: A classroom session teaching how words are written is named the same as one on casting charms.

clue.text: How to terminate the class system?

definitions.text: How to terminate the class system?

parts.words: How to terminate the class system?
parts.note: the class is a school class, and at the end of term the school dismisses its pupils for the holidays; the surface suggests abolishing social classes

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to dissolve or disperse, as a school does when term ends and classes disperse.

clue.text: Arranged as commanded

definitions.meaning: arranged means put in sequence or sorted
what was commanded was instructed or decreed

explanation.surface: Something set out exactly as instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both put in sequence and instructed by authority.

clue.text: Rotten row

definitions.meaning: rotten means foul-smelling or putrid
a row of soldiers standing side by side in a line

explanation.surface: Rotten Row, the riding track through London's Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotten Row is a famous bridle path in Hyde Park, London; the clue splits the name into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foul-smelling and also a line of soldiers abreast.

clue.text: Free-style wrestling can leave one so exhausted

definitions.meaning: wrestling with few holds barred was billed by this name
exhausted means tired out, worn out

explanation.surface: No-holds-barred grappling can leave a fighter worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names wrestling without restrictions and, informally, means completely worn out.

clue.text: Extremely light overhead

definitions.meaning: extremely means to a high degree
a coloured signal flare fired up from a pistol is named after its American inventor Edward Wilson ...

explanation.surface: A strong lamp in the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare fired from a pistol into the sky, named after its inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to a great degree and also names the pistol-fired signal flare that bursts in the sky.

clue.text: Smith's equipment essential to the listener

definitions.meaning: a blacksmith hammers hot metal on a heavy iron block
one of the three tiny bones of the middle ear, the incus, is named for its shape

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's kit that is indispensable to someone hearing him work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listener' suggests a person; the essential part is in the ear, where the incus, one of three small bones, carries this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The blacksmith's iron block and a small bone in the middle ear share this name.

clue.text: Emotionally strained verbal form

definitions.meaning: emotionally strained means anxious, on edge
in grammar, a form of a verb showing time, such as past or future

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about getting their grammar right.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means anxious and stretched tight, and also names the grammatical time of a verb.

clue.text: Seasonably promising advice to a bounder

definitions.meaning: the feeling that warmer weather and new growth are on the way
a bounder is read as one who bounds or jumps, who is told to leap upwards

explanation.surface: A hopeful forecast, with a tip for a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: A bounder is old British slang for a cad, but here it is one who bounds, so the advice is to jump.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the hopeful mood of the coming season and also tells a jumper to leap upwards.

clue.text: Doubly expensive expression of regret

indicators.note: doubly means the word is given two times in a row

explanation.surface: Sighing over a purchase that cost twice what it should.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is a mild cry of dismay or sorrow.

clue.text: Getting away from it all by working on firemen's equipment

definitions.meaning: fleeing or breaking free
constructing an external staircase for leaving a burning building

explanation.surface: Escaping everyday life by tinkering with a fire engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the phrase as building a fire-escape, the staircase on the outside of a building, with 'fire' supplied by 'firemen's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fleeing, and also constructing a staircase used in a fire.

clue.text: Adam's Thames-side property

parts.note: the Adam brothers, Scottish architects, built a riverside terrace development in London off the Strand, named from the Greek for brothers

explanation.definitionFit: The Georgian housing scheme by the Thames was designed and built by Robert and James Adam.

clue.text: A powerful moral tale of courteous description

parts.note: f stands for forte, the musical direction to play loudly or powerfully
a short story with a moral, like Aesop's

explanation.surface: A forceful parable about good manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone friendly and pleasant is polite and gracious in manner.

clue.text: A boon to the thirsty in Devon

definitions.meaning: a pint of ale is welcome to someone thirsty
a fishing village on the Devon coast in south-west England carries this name

explanation.surface: Something welcome to parched travellers in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; one of its coastal villages has this name, so the drink and the place share it.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink quenches thirst, and the same name belongs to a seaside village in Devon.

clue.text: The philosopher at the breakfast table?

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., the Elizabethan philosopher and statesman
cured pork rashers are a breakfast staple

explanation.surface: A great thinker sitting down to his morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was an English thinker, and the cured pork shares his surname.

clue.text: About to transgress? It's a sticky subject!

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in letters
to sin is to transgress a moral law

explanation.surface: A warning about wrongdoing, labelled a touchy topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sticky subject' reads as an awkward topic; the subject is literally sticky, tree gum.
explanation.definitionFit: The gummy substance oozed by pine trees is tacky to the touch.

clue.text: At a distance after a flying service returns

indicators.note: after places the turned-round service behind the letter from a
returns signals that the service's initials are read backwards

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's flying service

explanation.surface: Someone far away after an air force flight comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is the flying service; 'flying' tempts a solver to look for an anagram, but it is part of the definition of the service.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far off is a long way away.

clue.text: Noah's eldest son confused by hole in net

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the son's name is put in a new order

parts.note: Shem is traditionally Noah's eldest son in Genesis

explanation.surface: Noah's firstborn baffled by a gap in a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening between the cords of a net is a single gap in the netting.

clue.text: Goodfellow joins sailor in having a common try at it

parts.note: a good fellow is a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Robin Goodfellow teams up with a sailor in a shared attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodfellow' suggests Robin Goodfellow, the sprite Puck, but read as 'good fellow' it is a saint, ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is, colloquially, to have a go or attempt at it.

clue.text: Messages in code? Mere nothings

definitions.meaning: coded messages are encrypted writing
zeros, figures with no value, so people of no importance

explanation.surface: Wondering whether secret messages amount to anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means encrypted messages and also zeros, people of no account.

clue.text: Distinguished but incapable

definitions.meaning: distinguished means eminent or worth noticing
incapable split as ..., unable

explanation.surface: Someone eminent yet inept.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into two words: NOT ABLE, unable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means eminent, and split in two it means unable.

clue.text: Sounding negative in stable surroundings

parts.note: saying nay is giving a negative answer, and the horse's cry in its stall sounds just like it

explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a horse in its stall sounds like someone saying nay.

clue.text: Dim-sighted second-rate Shakespearean monarch

parts.note: B grade is second class, second-rate
King Lear is the title role of Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A poor-quality production of a Shakespeare king with failing eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucester, not Lear, is blinded in the play, but the old king's dim vision suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are watery and unfocused, so sight is dimmed.
